Git found no common ancestor between the two branches, so it can’t treat them as parts of the same project history. This often happens when you merge two separately created repositories, or when a remote repository was initialized with its own commit (such as a README).

If you intended to combine them, Git can be told to proceed:

```bash
git pull origin main --allow-unrelated-histories
```

Replace `main` with the relevant branch. Git may then ask you to resolve conflicts. If you didn’t expect two separate histories, check your remote and branch first rather than forcing the merge.
